question.text: Which of the following statements about a buyback of shares is INCORRECT?

answer.text: Shares bought back are extinguished and cannot be reissued
Buyback is regulated by SEBI (Buy-Back of Securities) Regulations 2018
Buyback is mandatory for all listed companies with surplus cash
Buyback involves repurchase of shares from existing shareholders

explanation.text: The Logic: A buyback is a corporate action in which a company repurchases its own shares from existing shareholders. Per the workbook, buyback of listed-company shares is governed by the SEBI (Buy-Back of Securities) Regulations, participation by shareholders is voluntary, and the shares bought back are extinguished. There is no requirement that a listed company with surplus cash must undertake a buyback, so the "mandatory" statement is incorrect. The Trap: Options A, B and D each restate features the workbook actually attributes to buybacks (extinguishment, the governing SEBI regulations, and repurchase from existing shareholders). The single word "mandatory" in Option C is what makes it the incorrect statement, since buybacks are always voluntary. Note: Limit your reasoning to the source-supported features (voluntary participation, extinguishment, SEBI Buy-Back Regulations, repurchase from existing shareholders). The workbook pages checked here do not characterise buybacks as signals of undervaluation or comment on debt-funded buybacks.
